raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The CPU override was called positionally, so block_size received the slot-mapping tensor and the block-size assert failed.

## Claims

- Fixes `RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous` in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` during `execute_model` on CPU when Triton is unavailable.
- The override now uses the same parameter names and order as `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher forwards launch kwargs by name.
- `KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE` is passed to the C++ op, and slots past `num_tokens` are filled with `PAD_ID`. Context parallelism is still rejected on CPU.


## Validation

- Compared the parameter lists of `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` and `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`. They match in name and order.
- No new test was added. This path runs only when Triton is unavailable, and the failure was observed on an s390x CPU serve of `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b`.
- After this change, rebuild and serve on that CPU. One chat request should get past `compute_slot_mapping` without the boolean-tensor assert.

## Details

`KernelOverride` forwards by keyword only when the replacement function's parameter names equal the Triton kernel's `arg_names`. The CPU function used `query_start_loc`, `block_size`, and `BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK`, while the kernel uses `query_start_loc_ptr`, `slot_mapping_ptr`, and `KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE`. The mismatch sent the slot-mapping tensor into `block_size`, and `assert block_size * BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK == KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE` could not reduce a multi-element boolean tensor.
The fix stays in the CPU fallback. The Triton kernel and the C++ slot-mapping op are unchanged. The C++ op still does not implement context parallelism; `TOTAL_CP_WORLD_SIZE != 1` continues to raise.

---

</details>

nodes.body: @bigPYJ1151 can you take a look at this PR. Thanks!

Hi @R3hankhan123, thanks for looking into this CPU fallback issue. I opened #61151 on October 12 to fix the same failure reported in #61131.

The core signature fix overlaps: both PRs align the fallback's parameter names and order with `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, remove the obsolete arguments, and pass `KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE` to the existing C++ operator.

#61151 already includes:

- Two native CPU regression cases through the real warmup launch and `KernelOverride`, covering a single request and multiple requests crossing a KV-block boundary; both fail before the fix and pass afterward.
- Registration of the regression test in the x86 CPU job and ARM CPU test script.
- macOS arm64 end-to-end validation, plus independent [Linux x86_64 retesting](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61151#issuecomment-6136950323) and [OPT-125m validation on a newer main on macOS](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61151#issuecomment-6173913422), with generated token IDs matching the Transformers reference.

Could we coordinate around #61151 for the signature fix to avoid maintaining two overlapping PRs? The additional tail-padding behavior here could be discussed and tested separately, particularly the `num_tokens < max_num_tokens` case, since it is outside #61151's scope. Happy to coordinate with you and the maintainers on how to split that work.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @R3hankhan123.

@@ -12,30 +12,30 @@
 def _compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl(
     num_tokens: int,
     max_num_tokens: int,
-    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs + 1], int32
-    positions: torch.Tensor,  # [num_tokens], int64
-    block_table: torch.Tensor,  # [max_num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req], int32
-    block_table_stride: int,  # max_num_blocks_per_req
-    block_size: int,
-    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,  # [max_num_tokens], int64
-    KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE: int | None = None,
-    BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK: int = 1,
-    TOTAL_CP_WORLD_SIZE: int = 1,
-    TOTAL_CP_RANK: int = 0,
-    CP_KV_CACHE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE: int = 1,
-    PAD_ID: int = -1,
-    BLOCK_SIZE: int = 1024,
+    query_start_loc_ptr: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs + 1], int32
+    positions_ptr: torch.Tensor,  # [num_tokens], int64
+    block_table_ptr: torch.Tensor,  # [max_num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req], int32
+    block_table_stride: int,
+    slot_mapping_ptr: torch.Tensor,  # [max_num_tokens], int64
+    KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE: int,
+    TOTAL_CP_WORLD_SIZE: int,
+    TOTAL_CP_RANK: int,
+    CP_KV_CACHE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE: int,
+    PAD_ID: int,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: int,
 ) -> None:
+    del TOTAL_CP_RANK, CP_KV_CACHE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE
     assert TOTAL_CP_WORLD_SIZE == 1, "Context Parallelism is not supported on CPU."
-    if BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK != 1:
-        assert block_size * BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK == KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE
+    assert block_table_stride == block_table_ptr.stride(0)
     torch.ops._C.compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl(
-        query_start_loc,
-        positions,
-        block_table,
-        slot_mapping,
-        block_size,
+        query_start_loc_ptr,
+        positions_ptr,
+        block_table_ptr,
+        slot_mapping_ptr,
+        KV_CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE,
     )
+    if num_tokens < max_num_tokens:
+        slot_mapping_ptr[num_tokens:max_num_tokens].fill_(PAD_ID)
